title: OpenAI's Sam Altman says 'AI authoritarianism' is one of his big fears
excerpt: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he's worried that the most advanced AI could controlled by a small number of companies or countries that gatekeep the tech.
content_html:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman says one of his biggest concerns about AI isn't whether it becomes too powerful in and of itself, but that a single company could control that power.

"I think the fight of the current moment is: Are we going to head to a world of AI authoritarianism or liberty?" Altman said on the latest episode of the "Relentless" podcast.

"Every time that humanity has traded off its liberty for safety, it's been a long-term net loss," Altman said. "We are going to put this in the hands of people. We're going to empower them. We are going to let society express its ideas and use this technology in the way they want."

It's a striking argument from the head of OpenAI, one of a small number of companies that control the world's most powerful AI models. OpenAI is also proprietary rather than open-source, meaning it doesn't share its tech.

Altman's comments are well-timed. They follow a debate that erupted in Silicon Valley and Washington last week over how much visibility the general public should have into the architecture of frontier models.

The recent release of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3, a powerful Chinese open-source model, sparked calls from some US officials to restrict access to Chinese models — and warnings from investors and startup founders that doing so could weaken global competition.

The divide extends beyond model access. US export controls already determine which countries and companies can obtain the most advanced chips and computing capacity, giving Washington significant influence over who can build cutting-edge AI.

Microsoft, Meta, Nvidia, OpenAI, Google, and many other leading tech companies signed a letter urging Washington not to restrict open-source AI.

Anthropic, OpenAI's biggest competitor and arguably the leading AI company on the planet right now, was the only major frontier lab that neither signed the letter nor publicly supported its contents. The company is known for taking a more cautious approach — arguing that increasingly capable models require stronger safeguards and tighter controls.

Altman, meanwhile, said preventing such power from becoming overly concentrated has long been central to his vision for AI, even as his company continues to keep its own models closed.

"For so long now, I have felt focused on this singular goal of abundant intelligence and a belief that incredible human prosperity will come from that, as long as we don't have a weird power concentration and kind of a new authoritarianism," he said.

content_html_zh:
OpenAI 首席执行官 Sam Altman 表示，他对人工智能最大的担忧之一不是它本身是否变得太强大，而是一家公司可以控制这种力量。

“我认为当前的斗争是：我们将走向人工智能独裁主义还是自由的世界？” 奥特曼在最新一集的“无情”播客中说道。

“每当人类为了安全而牺牲自由时，这都是长期的净损失，”奥特曼说。 “我们将把它交给人们。 我们将赋予他们权力。 我们将让社会表达自己的想法，并以他们想要的方式使用这项技术。”

这是 OpenAI 负责人的一个引人注目的论点，OpenAI 是控制世界上最强大人工智能模型的少数公司之一。 OpenAI 也是专有的而不是开源的，这意味着它不共享其技术。

奥特曼的评论恰逢其时。 上周在硅谷和华盛顿爆发了一场关于公众应该对前沿模型架构有多少可见度的辩论。

Moonshot AI 的 Kimi K3（一种强大的中国开源模型）最近发布，引发了一些美国官员呼吁限制使用中国模型，投资者和初创公司创始人也警告称，这样做可能会削弱全球竞争。

这种鸿沟超出了模型访问的范围。 美国的出口管制已经决定了哪些国家和公司可以获得最先进的芯片和计算能力，这使华盛顿对谁可以构建尖端人工智能具有重大影响力。

微软、Meta、Nvidia、OpenAI、谷歌和许多其他领先科技公司签署了一封信，敦促华盛顿不要限制开源人工智能。

Anthropic 是 OpenAI 最大的竞争对手，可以说是目前全球领先的人工智能公司，它是唯一一家既没有签署这封信，也没有公开支持其内容的主要前沿实验室。 该公司以采取更加谨慎的态度而闻名——认为功能日益强大的模型需要更强有力的保障措施和更严格的控制。

与此同时，奥尔特曼表示，防止这种权力过度集中一直是他人工智能愿景的核心，尽管他的公司继续保持自己的模型封闭。

他说：“长期以来，我一直专注于丰富智慧这一单一目标，并相信只要我们没有奇怪的权力集中和新的独裁主义，人类就会实现令人难以置信的繁荣。”
